findings.evidence:
pruned = _prune(dest, errors)
    ok = verified and not errors
findings.counterexample: 14 complete generations exist. The next run creates a new *-dr-alex.bundle then fails the sqlite snapshot (SQLITE_BUSY) and/or private archive. _prune still keeps the 14 newest bundles and deletes the oldest stem's .bundle, -state.db.enc, and -private.tar.gz.enc. Fourteen later incomplete runs leave only shells with no decryptable state/private payload.
findings.fix: Treat a generation as retained only when bundle verify, snapshot (if db exists), and private archive all succeed; prune that set. On failure, delete the new stem's artifacts and do not consume a retention slot.

findings.counterexample: git bundle create writes directly to dest/{ts}-dr-alex.bundle and then early-returns without unlink or prune. A leftover truncated/invalid bundle stays in dest.glob("*-dr-alex.bundle"). Every later run sets verified=False on bundle verify of that file, so ok is never True while that file remains (until 15+ bundles exist and it ages out).
findings.fix: Create the bundle at a temp path, verify that file, then os.replace onto {ts}-dr-alex.bundle. On create/verify failure, unlink the temp/partial file before return.

findings.counterexample: Live state.db is snapshotted with sqlite3.backup into the tar as data/state.db, but state.db-journal is still a regular file and is archived beside it. Restore of both into the same directory can make SQLite replay the live journal against the backup copy (different pager state), corrupting the recovered DB. WAL/SHM were excluded for this reason; DELETE-mode journals were not.
findings.fix: Also skip names ending in -journal (and do not raw-add sqlite sidecars). Keep using backup() for the closed main DB file only.

findings.counterexample: A records/continuity file that is a symlink (iCloud/external path) is skipped, so it is absent from the encrypted tar. Active File is handled later without that skip: archive.add(active, arcname="records/Active-File.md", recursive=False) stores a symlink member when active is a symlink, so restore recreates a pointer, not the file bytes, and off-this-tree targets are missing.
findings.fix: For private members, lstat; if a symlink, open/copy the referent's bytes into the tar under the intended arcname (fail that file if the referent is unreadable). Do not emit symlink members as the restore payload.

findings.counterexample: On Python 3.12, Path.rglob follows directory symlinks. data/exfil -> /elsewhere makes regular files under /elsewhere appear as data/exfil/... (is_symlink() is false on those files). They are packed into the Fernet tar. This is not zip-slip on extract (arcname stays under data/ or records/), but it is the concrete traversal/symlink hole in assembly. Cyclic dir links can also hang sorted(rglob) until the 120s git timeout is irrelevant.
findings.fix: Walk with follow_symlinks/recurse_symlinks disabled (or scandir without following dirs); skip any dir whose path is a symlink. Keep refusing file symlinks unless you copy referent bytes as in the previous fix.

findings.evidence:
One command produces two durable artifacts under ``data/backups/``
...
class BackupResult:
    ok: bool
    bundle_path: str | None = None
    snapshot_path: str | None = None
    private_archive_path: str | None = None
    verified: bool = False
findings.counterexample: A green/silent BackupResult cannot be turned back into a running app: verified is only git bundle verify; there is no recorded statedb.state_db_path() or config.records_dir(); private files are stored under generic data/ and records/ prefixes (Active File forced to records/Active-File.md). Restore to the wrong path misses what the process actually reads. The implemented third artifact is also omitted from the module contract text.
findings.fix: Keep the three artifacts, but persist a sibling manifest (original db path, records dir, active-file path, stems) and document decrypt+extract+git clone --mirror from the bundle. Set verified from all checks you already run, not only git.

findings.counterexample: If chmod 0700 fails, mkdir leaves a umask dir (often 0755). The git bundle is never chmod 0600 (only the .enc files are). Other local accounts can then read the plaintext --all bundle from data/backups/. Encrypted blobs stay ciphertext; the bundle is source.
findings.fix: Do not swallow chmod failure on dest; chmod the bundle to 0600 like the .enc files (or fail the run).

limitations: Only this module was supplied: no restore CLI/tests, no bodies for statedb.state_db_path, config.records_dir, config.active_file_path, or crypto.encrypt_bytes.
Point-in-time is intended: committed WAL at backup() is in scope; later transactions are not.
Fernet key remaining in the user Keychain is an explicit boundary; same-Mac restore cannot prove separate off-device key custody.
Did not claim other private stores exist unless this file walks them; coverage was judged from the two roots plus Active File only.
